factProposals.value: A process analysis dashboard (web pages served locally) showing the latest analysis's headline, counts, automation opportunities, bottlenecks and duplicated work, a table of every completed analysis, and each analysis's full report including method and limitations.

The dashboard reads only the reports the analysis service saved; analyses that never produced a report (missing data, interrupted) are not shown, and damaged saved records are skipped and counted on the page.
Only the data analyst, process analyst and operations manager roles may view the dashboard; anyone not signed in gets 401 and any other role 403, and neither sees any data.

Every dashboard request (sign-in, sign-out, page views, refusals, not-found, data and rendering errors) is written to the hash-chained audit log with the user id or "anonymous" and a timestamp; page views record which analyses were shown. The entry is written before the page is sent, and if it cannot be written no data is shown. Pages carry a Content Security Policy that blocks all scripts.
If the saved analyses cannot be read the dashboard returns a 503 'could not load' page; if a page cannot be built it returns a complete 500 error page, never part of a page.
The data analyst role appears as a dashboard viewer alongside the process analyst and operations manager.

decisions.statement: Build the dashboard as a small server-side web app rather than a tab in the static Command Center.
decisions.rationale: A static public page cannot check who is viewing or write to the audit log, so it could not meet the unauthorised-access path or the logging criterion.

decisions.statement: Use a clearly labelled demo sign-in (user id and role kept in a cookie) as a stand-in for real authentication.
decisions.rationale: The project has no login system yet. Chosen by the student before building; the permission check and audit trail are real.

decisions.statement: Allow the data analyst, process analyst and operations manager roles.
decisions.rationale: The data analyst owns the story; the other two already run analyses. Chosen by the student before building.

decisions.statement: Add a read-only list() to the result stores and share role-name matching in src/lib/roles.js.
decisions.rationale: The dashboard must list saved analyses, which the stores could not do; one shared role rule stops the dashboard and the analysis service disagreeing about who a role is. Both changes approved by the student.

decisions.statement: Read each request address exactly as sent, so an address starting with "//" is a path (404) rather than another host.
decisions.rationale: Found by a randomised stress test: "//x/..." was read as host x, path "/...", so the server answered addresses it should not and logged the wrong address.

decisions.statement: Show a generic "could not load" message on the 503 page and keep the underlying error (which can name files) in the audit log only.
decisions.rationale: Found in code review: the raw storage error exposed internal file paths to users.

limitations.statement: Sign-in is not authentication: the user id and role are whatever was typed, and the cookie is not signed. Anyone who can reach the server can claim an allowed role.
The server listens on 127.0.0.1 only and has no HTTPS; it is a local tool, not yet deployable for other people.
The data-read time limit only takes effect for a store that reads over a network; today's file store reads synchronously (a corrupted file is still caught).
Every request is audited, including browser requests such as /favicon.ico, so the log includes some not-found entries that are not user actions.
The dashboard has only been shown synthetic analyses; no real organisation's data has been displayed.

There is no rate limiting: anyone who can reach the server can send many requests, each writing an audit entry (addresses are cut to 200 characters). Because the audit log refuses all writes after a failed one, a full disk takes the dashboard down until restart. Acceptable while it listens on 127.0.0.1 only.
